sources.title: Socio-Economic Impact Assessment of Dzud 2023-2024: Dzud Resilience Strategy Policy Recommendations
sources.organization: UNDP Mongolia, in collaboration with the Government of Mongolia and partner agencies
sources.temporal_coverage: Assesses the 2023-2024 dzud; the PDF cover says September 2024 and the UNDP publication page is dated 27 May 2025. Field survey data were collected in 2024; the risk map cited is dated 20 December 2023.
sources.methodology: Uses NEMA/NAMEM records, field visits and ADAPT household survey.
sources.limitations: Survey covers four aimags; conflict observations are not armed-conflict estimates.

sources.title: 2024 Dzud Early Action and Response Plan
sources.organization: United Nations Resident Coordinator's Office and Humanitarian Country Team, Mongolia
sources.temporal_coverage: Plan issued 19 February 2024 for the December 2023-May 2024 dzud response; targeting criteria and actions refer to that event period.
sources.methodology: HCT plan synthesizes government dzud-risk classifications and sector response inputs.
sources.limitations: Plan targets and reported early actions are not a final coverage audit.

sources.title: Mongolia Humanitarian Situation Report No. 4 (Dzud), 30 April 2024
sources.temporal_coverage: Situation report dated 30 April 2024; impact figures cover the November 2023-April 2024 dzud, with programme outputs stated through 25 April 2024.
sources.methodology: UNICEF situation report compiles needs data and agency-reported programme results.
sources.limitations: Snapshot is dated 30 April 2024; output counts are time-bound and not outcome evaluations.

sources.title: World Bank Report Highlights Importance of Social Protection Response in Strengthening Mongolian Households' Resilience to Climate and Economic Shocks
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank press release dated 27 May 2025 summarizing a report on adaptive social protection and herder resilience.
sources.methodology: Publisher summary of a World Bank study of adaptive social protection.
sources.limitations: Full report link did not open; evidence is limited to the official summary.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.63 (printed p.60), 20 December 2023 soum-level dzud risk map; and physical p.38 (printed p.35), Table 5, livestock losses by herd size and aimag.
claims.paraphrase: December 2023 risk mapping rated 90% of territory high or very high risk; surveyed herders with under 200 animals lost 61% in Sukhbaatar versus 6% in Khovd.
institutions: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring
claims.limitations: Historical map; the household survey covers four aimags, not all Mongolia.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.47-48 (printed pp.44-45), dzud-related migration; physical p.80 (printed p.77), pastureland condition and Otor movement.
claims.paraphrase: Dzud losses prompt migration to cities or other aimags; urban resource competition can cause conflict, while degraded pasture draws herders to Otor land and conflict with locals.
claims.limitations: The report gives no conflict counts or armed-conflict classification.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Assessment links dzud migration and pasture access with resource-competition conflict.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.49-50 (printed pp.46-47), migration and gender-based violence sections.
claims.paraphrase: SEIA identifies gender-based violence in dzud-affected households alongside health problems and schooling disruption.
claims.limitations: The cited assessment provides no pre-dzud comparison of GBV prevalence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report lists GBV among the 2023-2024 dzud's social impacts.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.14 (printed p.11), executive summary on warning and local response capacity.
claims.paraphrase: Herders received dzud warnings, but community response remained limited by inaccessible pasture and shortages of trained staff and equipment.
institutions: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring
claims.limitations: Event-period assessment; later capacity changes were not evaluated.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.9 (printed p.9), vulnerability profile and targeting criteria.
claims.paraphrase: Plan prioritizes herder households with 100-400 livestock units, limited basic services, pregnant or lactating women, single parents, disabled members or widowed elders.
claims.limitations: These are 2024 humanitarian criteria, not a current household registry.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.6-7 (printed pp.6-7), monitoring and dzud risk-map description.
claims.paraphrase: Government risk maps combined remote sensing and ground observations of snow, drought, pasture productivity, livestock numbers and carrying capacity to guide early action.
affected_groups: soums at high or extreme dzud risk
institutions: National Agency for Meteorology and Environmental Monitoring
claims.limitations: Plan describes the 2023-2024 process, not its predictive accuracy.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.3 and 10 (printed pp.3 and 10), assistance target and reported government response actions.
claims.paraphrase: The plan aimed to assist 33,400 of 150,500 people identified in need and reported discounted hay and fodder for high-risk provinces.
claims.limitations: Target population and reported actions do not establish final reach or outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.1 (printed p.1), Situation in Numbers and impact summary.
claims.paraphrase: The 2023-2024 dzud affected over 188,300 people, including 80,215 children; two of 20 reported deaths were children.
claims.limitations: Situation counts are as of the report's 30 April 2024 date.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.1 (printed p.1), household coping and child wellbeing observations.
claims.paraphrase: Rural herder women and children faced malnutrition risks as families cut spending on check-ups, education, hygiene and warm clothes; UNICEF observed child mental distress.
claims.limitations: The report does not quantify district-level child outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF physical pp.2 and 3 (printed pp.2 and 3), health outreach and road-clearing response.
claims.paraphrase: By 25 April, mobile health services reached 141,873 people in high-risk areas, including young children, pregnant women and persons with disabilities; road support covered 78 soums in 11 provinces.
claims.limitations: These are cumulative reported outputs, not impact evaluations.

claims.locator: PDF physical p.2 (printed p.2), child protection and gender-based violence response section.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF was organizing emergency child-protection training for 320 local responders and refresher support for rapid-response teams and community groups addressing GBV.
claims.limitations: Training and support were ongoing; the report does not measure resulting capacity change.

claims.locator: World Bank publisher page, report summary, resilience evidence and recommendations.
claims.paraphrase: World Bank summary says social protection expanded during COVID-19 and recommends adaptive disaster plans, better household data systems and advance payments for herders facing dzud.
claims.limitations: The page summarizes a report; recommendations are not evidence of reform implementation.

access_audit.notes: Read the full report PDF directly; verified cover and preferred citation dates against the UNDP publication page dated 27 May 2025.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Report states all rights reserved and requires prior permission for reproduction.

access_audit.notes: Read the complete public plan; cover states issued 19 February 2024 and plan period December 2023-May 2024.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No license terms identified in inspected pages.

access_audit.notes: Directly opened UNICEF situation report; date and output cutoff are stated in the PDF.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No license terms identified in inspected pages.

search_audit.query: site:unfccc.int Mongolia NDC climate vulnerability aimag drought dzud herders PDF
search_audit.outcome: Read UNDP's 2023-24 dzud assessment, the 2024 response plan and UNICEF's dated situation report for aimag, soum and household-level findings.

search_audit.query: Mongolia dzud herder household poverty local conflict water pasture report World Bank PDF
search_audit.outcome: The UNDP assessment links dzud-related migration and pasture access to resource-competition conflict and identifies GBV among social impacts; no armed-conflict estimate was found.

search_audit.query: Mongolia climate displacement social conflict herders mining conflict report UNDP PDF
search_audit.outcome: Search and direct source review found dzud migration/resource competition and GBV pathways, but no source-stated armed attack or insecurity interrupting a named climate-adaptation activity.

search_audit.query: Mongolia local climate adaptation resilience capacity early warning dzud pastoral communities government report
search_audit.outcome: Read government/HCT anticipatory-risk mapping and response targeting, UNICEF's operational outputs, UNDP's capacity findings and the World Bank's official social-protection summary.

gaps: No directly read source established climate-related effects on armed conflict or insecurity interrupting a named adaptation project; resource-competition conflict and GBV are recorded only as the reports describe them.
The UNFCCC National Adaptation Plan PDF timed out, and the UN Mongolia 2024 Common Country Analysis exceeded the reader limit; neither report's indexed text was used as evidence.
The World Bank's full social-protection study link returned an unexpected status; its claim is limited to the directly opened World Bank summary.
The FAO early-action policy-brief PDF redirected to an inaccessible reader; the brief was not used for claims.
The response and UNICEF situation reports describe the 2023-2024 dzud and are historical evidence, not statements of conditions or programme status in 2026.
